# Conditional compute: choose experts, skip work, or retrieve stored knowledge?

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/foundation-models/conditional-compute.md) · English

Updated 2026-10-27 · 26 topic entries / 6 representative comparisons

Parameter capacity, active computation per token, and serving latency are distinct. Switch selects experts; Engram and Memory Grafting retrieve local patterns. AdaDSF, Telescopic LM, and WIDE allocate work by token and layer, full depth, and group width respectively. Identify the routing unit before discussing capacity or savings.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Expert computation and conditional memory are different capacities

Switch executes a nonlinear expert on the hidden input. Engram retrieves discrete local-pattern entries and gates them by context. Memory Grafting gets some entries from frozen offline pretrained representations. Sparse capacity therefore means different things for expert weights, learned tables, and frozen banks. Expected constant-time addressing does not eliminate lookup transfer and fusion costs.

Sources: [Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity](../../../../reproductions/2101.03961-switch-transformer/README-en.md) · [Conditional Memory via Scalable Lookup: A New Axis of Sparsity for Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2601.07372-engram/README-en.md) · [Memory Grafting: Scaling Language Model Pre-training via Offline Conditional Memory](../../../../reproductions/2605.20948-memory-grafting/README-en.md)

### State the unit of a conditional budget

AdaDSF sets how many tokens enter each layer; Telescopic LM runs a complete depth prefix; WIDE selects each token's attention and FFN groups. Similar active ratios conceal different dependencies, workloads, and kernels. Dense computation followed by zero masking saves no latency. Consider training compatibility and actual deployment skip granularity.

Sources: [Adaptive Depth Sparse Framework: Similarity-Driven Resource Allocation for Pre-Trained LLMs](../../../../reproductions/2607.21291-adadsf/README-en.md) · [Telescopic Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2609.35769-telescopic-lm/README-en.md) · [WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning](../../../../reproductions/2607.28418-wide/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### What do a Switch expert and an Engram or Memory Grafting lookup add for a repeated phrase? {#cross-lookup-versus-expert}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Switch adds a routed function executed on the current hidden input. Engram learns discrete n-gram values; Memory Grafting reuses frozen external phrase representations with fallback. Conditional computation and local lookup both help capacity but do not guarantee compositional answers.

    **Illustrative example:** A repeated product name can retrieve a stable hint; comparing two products' uses still needs context and computation.

    Sources: [Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity](../../../../reproductions/2101.03961-switch-transformer/README-en.md) · [Conditional Memory via Scalable Lookup: A New Axis of Sparsity for Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2601.07372-engram/README-en.md) · [Memory Grafting: Scaling Language Model Pre-training via Offline Conditional Memory](../../../../reproductions/2605.20948-memory-grafting/README-en.md)

### Why do AdaDSF, Telescopic LM, and WIDE produce different execution graphs even at half the compute? {#cross-budget-unit}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** AdaDSF can route tokens differently across layers; Telescopic LM runs one complete prefix; WIDE routes groups within a layer per token. Equal averages do not fix slowest paths, group shapes, or memory traffic. Log token-layer assignment, actual depth, and group activation separately.

    **Illustrative example:** Half the tokens at full depth, all tokens at half depth, and each token at half width are different forward passes.

    Sources: [Adaptive Depth Sparse Framework: Similarity-Driven Resource Allocation for Pre-Trained LLMs](../../../../reproductions/2607.21291-adadsf/README-en.md) · [Telescopic Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2609.35769-telescopic-lm/README-en.md) · [WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning](../../../../reproductions/2607.28418-wide/README-en.md)

### Why can't Switch and WIDE speedups be inferred from mask counts? {#cross-sparsity-versus-latency}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Experts can require dispatch and imbalance handling; grouped masks need hardware skipping with different matrix and memory patterns. Dense computation then masking only changes values. Even genuine skips require counting routing, reordering, and communication. Measure the end-to-end workload.

    **Illustrative example:** Half the FFN channels can be slower if extra rearrangement and small matrix calls replace one efficient dense matrix.

    Sources: [Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity](../../../../reproductions/2101.03961-switch-transformer/README-en.md) · [WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning](../../../../reproductions/2607.28418-wide/README-en.md)
